verses.1: And David went up from there, and he sat down beside Eben-Edid.
verses.2: And it happened that Sheol returned from behind Philistia. They told him, “Look! David is in the valley of Eben-Gedi.”
verses.3: And Shaul took three thousand men, chosen from all of Israel. He went to ask for David and his men in front of the high priests.
verses.4: And he went to the sheep pens along the road. There was a village there. Shaul came and laid his feet on the ground. David and his men sat in the courtyards of the village.
verses.5: And the men of David said to him, “Look, today is the day when Jehovah has spoken to you. I will give you your demand in your hands. You may do with it as you see fit.” Then David got up and put on the cloak that belonged to Saul.
verses.6: And after that, David’s heart was filled with anger because he had taken away the wing of Saul.
verses.7: And he said to his people, “Alas for me! May Jehovah forbid that I do this. If I do this, then it will be because Jehovah has sent me as a prophet. But if I do not do this, then it will be because Jehovah does not want me to do this.”
verses.8: David tried to persuade his men with words, but they refused to go with Saul. Then Saul got up from his place and went his own way.
verses.9: And David rose up after that. He left the cave and called out to Shaul, saying, “My lord, king!” Then Shaul raised his hand, and David conquered the land. They bowed down in worship.
verses.10: And David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to what people say? Look, David is seeking your ruin.”
verses.11: See, today your eyes have seen what the LORD has given you today. He placed it in my hand in the valley, and said to me, “Kill him.” But I said, “I will not stretch out my hand against the Lord’s anointed.” For the Lord’s anointed is Jesus.
verses.12: And my father also saw that I had taken your wing in my hands. I have taken your wing, and I have not killed you. Know this: there is no evil or sin in my hands. I have not committed any sin against you. And you have taken my soul away from me.
verses.13: The LORD will judge between me and you. The LORD will take revenge on me from you. My hand shall not be with you anymore.
verses.14: When the former ruler said, “The wicked will be cast out; my hands will not be with you.”
verses.15: After whom did the king of Israel arise? After whom do you pursue? After the dead cat, after Pharaoh himself.
verses.16: And Jehovah will be judge between me and you. He will see and avenge my enemies, and he will judge me in your presence.
verses.17: And David said these words to Shaul. Shaul replied, “You are my son, David.” Then Shaul took his bow and bowed down.
verses.18: And he said to David, “You are righteous. You have forgiven me, for you have done me good. And I will forgive you in return.”
verses.19: And you have today shown me that you did something good for me. You saved me from the hands of Jehovah, and you did not kill me.
verses.20: And if someone finds their enemy and sends him away in a good way, then God will bless you with good things on this day, as He has done for me.
verses.21: And now I know that you will be the king who rules over Israel. And a queen has been given to you as your wife.
verses.22: And now, may the LORD have mercy on me! If you destroy my descendants from among the people, and if you erase my name from among the descendants of my father’s house.
verses.23: David went to visit Saul. Saul went to his house, and David and his men went up onto the roof.
